summary: Ferry County, WA tower built in the 1940s and abandoned in 1974; now described as gone. Sources disagree on design, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 15' treated timber L-5 tower (FFLOS and Firelookout); 15-foot timber tower with R-6 cab (WillhiteWeb); Firelookout also lists a possible 20' R-6 tower in the 1960s, marked with a question mark
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1974. FFLOS says now gone, Forest Lookouts says removed, and WillhiteWeb says the date of removal or burning is unknown.

visit.trail_note: One Mountaineers trip report from a Kettle Crest backpack trip describes the group going on an evening walk to Barnaby Butte and its former lookout site. No agency statement on access was found.

events.note: Sources say only 'the 1940s' (FFLOS, Firelookout, WillhiteWeb); 1940 is a placeholder for the decade
All three lookout pages give 1974 as the year it was abandoned
Registered November 9, 2012 with FFLOS, nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: built in the 1940s as a 15-foot treated timber L-5 tower; abandoned in 1974; now gone
evidence.quote: Built in the 1940s, this 15' treated timber L-5 tower was abandoned in 1974 and is now gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and Firelookout give a 15-foot L-5 tower; WillhiteWeb gives a 15-foot tower with an R-6 cab. Firelookout also lists a possible 1960s 20-foot R-6 tower with a question mark. Not resolved; all versions are kept.

notes_for_editor: Record matches sources on county, agency, elevation and gone status. Access and staffing are omitted because no source gives them; the trip report page shows 'Mon, Jun 27, 2022', which may be the trip or posting date and is not used in the story. The 1940 built year is a decade placeholder. Cab and tower design conflict is unresolved. FFLOS credits a 1972 photo (Rex Kamstra collection) but no image URL was read, so no photo entry.
